delta.legacy: POI 5.5.1 createSheet accepts a sheet name of 32 or more characters, and Excel refuses the file it writes.
delta.now: The XLSX writer enforces Excel's sheet-name rules (1..31 characters, none of \ / ? * [ ] :, no leading or trailing apostrophe, not History); the text formats and the builder keep the legacy freedom.

delta.legacy: TomlScheduleParser.cleanToJsonArray removed the comma of ",]" with a regular expression over the whole text, inside string cells too.
delta.now: The reader never edits string content: a cell containing ",]" is data.

delta.legacy: A sheet named twice in YAML merged its rows; a duplicate JSON or TOML sheet key kept the last; an array or object inside a cell became an empty cell; unknown top-level keys were ignored; an unrecognised file extension fell back to XLSX; the builder dropped a third verb.
delta.now: Each is reported: INPUT_DUPLICATE_SHEET, INPUT_SCHEMA, a warning for unknown top-level keys, INPUT_UNRECOGNIZED_FORMAT, and an error from the builder; every finding has its source location.

delta.legacy: The legacy DataFormatter used the default locale of the machine, so a number cell could read 1,5 or 1.5.
delta.now: Number text is formatted with Locale.ROOT everywhere, whatever the default locale.

delta.legacy: FW_BinaryFile=, FW_DBURL=, FW_DBUSER=, FW_DBPASS= and FW_SQL= were logged as stubs and skipped; FW_CSVFile= with FW_Separator= ran a deprecated reader whose keys collided with real keys and whose rows never reached the sheet; any other FW_ cell was logged as not implemented.
delta.now: The seven stub directives are UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY at their cell (csv-import, binary-file, database); an unknown FW_ cell is SPEC_UNKNOWN_DIRECTIVE with a spelling suggestion.

delta.legacy: FW_Optional and FW_RefineCodeExceptQuoted changed the last key issued anywhere, so as the first cell of a sheet they changed the previous sheet (a null pointer for the first sheet); the three prefix directives matched by prefix and ignored what followed.
delta.now: They apply to the previous value of their own sheet; with none it is SPEC_DIRECTIVE_WITHOUT_TARGET at the cell; text after FW_Optional, FW_RefineCodeExceptQuoted or FW_EMPTY_STRING is a warning and the directive still applies.

delta.legacy: FW_File= read its path relative to the process working directory, kept a byte order mark, and on a read error logged and issued an empty value.
delta.now: The path resolves against the scenario file's own directory, so a scenario travels with its files; strict UTF-8 with the byte order mark dropped; lines joined by a line feed with a final one, as before; an unreadable or invalid file is an error at the cell.

delta.legacy: The comment-stripping expression of FW_RefineCodeExceptQuoted backtracks exponentially on an unclosed double quote followed by many backslashes; sixty backslashes would not finish.
delta.now: A verbatim port with a character-read budget: a text over the budget is INPUT_LIMIT at its directive; ordinary long texts are refined as before.

delta.legacy: Incomplete FW_SheetNames and FW_CUSTOM_VAR rows were ignored silently; a non-integer FW_CUSTOM_VAR index threw NumberFormatException; an unknown FW_ sheet was dropped silently.
delta.now: Incomplete rows are warnings, a bad index is an error at its cell, the thirteen known control sheets are accepted (seven of them inert, as there), and any other FW_ sheet is a warning with a suggestion.

delta.legacy: The directive dispatcher matched by prefix and read what it could not parse as a default: an unreadable verb argument meant 1, an unknown subset mode or FW_Subsets(3) meant all subsets, a joiner with an empty operand or a lower-case multiplicity produced no rows, a flag with text in front of it was accepted by endsWith, a FW_ReplaceRE alone was ignored.
delta.now: Each of those is an error that names the accepted form (PLAN_DIRECTIVE_SYNTAX, PLAN_UNKNOWN_DIRECTIVE). Every directive of the 32 real workbooks still parses. The corpus does not prove that every input the permissive legacy grammar accepted is accepted here.

delta.legacy: White space changed the legacy meaning silently: FW_Combi( 2 ) was FW_Combi(1); FW_Cartes( A ) looked up a sheet named " A "; an FW_ReplaceRE without white space after its comma was ignored, and a second one on the same line ran into the first replacement (the greedy .*); FW_() G was read as FW_(); a flag cell with white space around it matched nothing.
delta.now: White space around tokens is insignificant and means what it would mean without it; inside quotes, patterns and sheet names it is kept. A replacement is a quoted literal, or quoted literals and exactly one sheet name joined with +, typed as prefix, sheet and suffix; forms the legacy expression misread are refused with the accepted form.

delta.legacy: The separator field of a joiner names a sheet whose first value separates; the pre-scan turned every unknown operand into an empty virtual sheet, so a literal ";" silently did nothing.
delta.now: Virtual sheets are still generated (cf.plan.autoGenerateMissingSheets), each with a PLAN_VIRTUAL_SHEET warning that names the separator rule; with generation off an unknown reference is an error.

delta.legacy: A flag before the sheet name of a headless row applied to the generated sheet without a word; endsWith accepted xFW_Exclude as the flag.
delta.now: The first is PLAN_AMBIGUOUS_TARGET naming the generated sheet; the second is PLAN_UNKNOWN_DIRECTIVE.

delta.legacy: Sheets, values and virtual sheets were numbered from one shared counter (virtual sheets after the last value).
delta.now: Byte-migration B06 and B08: data sheets are keys 1..S and virtual sheets S+1.. in the sheet namespace, values S+1..S+C in the value namespace; the census covers both; nothing is renumbered.

delta.legacy: The legacy processes logged to standard output through a Log4j console appender, mixed with their results.
delta.now: Reports go to standard output in a machine-readable form (text or XML), diagnostics to standard error; the packaged-jar tests parse the XML of every format.

delta.legacy: The Core read ./fw.properties at start, with credentials and paths, and acted on every key it knew; keys it did not know were ignored; a blank db.password fell back to CORE_DB_PASSWORD.
delta.now: Legacy files are imported explicitly (--legacy-config) below every cf.* source; each key is mapped, honoured, retired, inert, deferred to its owner package (pending, and a run refuses it), superseded or refused; unknown keys are refused; the environment is reported and never applied; secrets are redacted (legacy-settings.xml).

delta.legacy: With core.threading.parallelizeSubCombosIfPossible true, a generator of more than core.threading.parallelThreshold rows (10000) was consumed in chunks by virtual threads sharing the id counter, so the ids, the order of a table's rows and everything read in that order depended on scheduling.
delta.now: Rows come in the selected library's rank order however many there are, and ids follow that order, so a run is reproducible. The rows and their parents are those the legacy produced; only their order, and so their ids, can differ from a scheduling-dependent legacy run, and no test claims legacy ids above the threshold.

delta.decision: supplement to revision 2: k above n
delta.legacy: The parallel library's combinations threw for a size above the source size (seven of the 232 recorded library cases); the legacy Core never asked for one, because SheetWorker.buildGenerator returned the subsets of an empty list instead: one empty row.
delta.now: The algebra answers zero tuples for such a size and keeps negative sizes as errors; the seven recorded exceptions are checked as zero tuples. Generation keeps the legacy guard: FW_Combi with a size above its source gives one empty row, in the first pass and for every source row of a later pass.

delta.decision: supplement to revision 2: R-M03-SEMANTICS item 6, settled by the developer
delta.legacy: A joiner read an operand's second table when it had rows and the first table otherwise (memory store), or the second table whenever it existed, empty or not (PostgreSQL store): a sheet whose last pass left nothing lent its previous table, or nothing, depending on the store.
delta.now: A joiner reads the operand's final table, the one its last directive left, as every other reader does; an empty final table gives the joiner no rows, as the PostgreSQL store did.

delta.legacy: With distinctify__fwX_Y__Tables the PostgreSQL store rebuilt a table from MIN(combi_id) and the row content, so the parent column fcombi_id came back empty; the memory store kept the first row whole.
delta.now: Content alone decides what repeats, and the first row of every content is kept whole, its id and parent id included, in table order (the memory store's result).

delta.legacy: A later pass read the first table into a map by id: the memory store let the last row with an id win, while the PostgreSQL store ordered by id only, so which of several rows sharing an id won was up to the database. Ids repeat when a joiner follows a swap.
delta.now: The last row with an id, in table order, wins, as in the memory store.

delta.legacy: SeqParser stored the text after FW_Concatenator= in key2concat, which nothing read: the Core and the Reader wrote a row's values back to back whatever the flag said, while the authoring layer (fwgen verb_max_row_arity, bundle/coverage.py) described it as the glue between them.
delta.now: FW_Concatenator=X joins the values of one row of that sheet (cf.render.sheetConcatenator=apply, the default); cf.render.sheetConcatenator=legacy-ignore writes them back to back as the legacy did. No workbook of the corpus uses the flag.

delta.legacy: The sieve decoded an empty mandatory fw_final cell, a present empty row as well as a NULL, as the baseline's values, and when the base row itself was empty it fell back to the spec's first value.
delta.now: A present empty row is an empty selection; a baseline reference resolves to the baseline row, even when that row is empty; no first value is invented (ASSEMBLY_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE when a sheet has no first row). The Reader rendered these rows the same way.

delta.legacy: A mandatory sheet whose table ended empty was dropped from the key maps, so the run went on with a weaker product; an empty source still in the product aborted fw_final; a plan without mandatory tables wrote no fw_final row at all.
delta.now: cf.generation.emptyStagePolicy=PRESERVE_EMPTY (default): a required sheet without rows leaves zero candidates with ASSEMBLY_EMPTY_FACTOR naming it; LEGACY_DROP_WITH_DIAGNOSTIC reproduces the drop with ASSEMBLY_SHEET_DROPPED. A plan without mandatory sheets has one structural empty tuple, which optional sheets expand.

delta.legacy: Rules touching an optional sheet were compiled to code tuples for the Reader's OptionalBondFilter, whose require and gate semantics differ from the sieve's, and absence-sensitive conditions (hasnt, ne, present, ordinal, countLe...) were refused (fail closed).
delta.now: One evaluator with the sieve's row_violations semantics checks every rule on the assembled candidate, absent sheets included, so absence-sensitive rules work; rules reading only mandatory sheets still run once per mandatory row first. Legacy compiled bonds files keep the Reader filter's own semantics.

delta.legacy: The Reader emitted the final-only pass and then final x fw_opt pairs from chunked, parallel drivers, so the order of candidates (and, with several COPY consumers or asynchronous optional inserts, their combination ids) depended on scheduling; the sink tag and the file tag of one candidate differed (finalId_optId_0 versus finalId_optId_k).
delta.now: One deterministic order: the absent branch of every mandatory row, then each optional size ascending, every mandatory row with every optional row of that size; display ids are the ids a single-threaded legacy run gave (finalId_0_0, finalId_optId_k).

delta.legacy: OptionalBondFilter ignored an unreadable bonds file or one with a malformed number, and skipped lines with too few fields; the sieve skipped rules naming fewer than two sheets unless asked to be strict.
delta.now: Constraint files are read strictly with the legacy strict loader's checks: every problem is an error with its location (CONSTRAINT_*), and no authored rule is dropped.

delta.legacy: t-wise reduction refused a spec with a constraint sidecar, flagged mandatory slots or verbs other than FW_Combi(1), because it covered raw values.
delta.now: Covering selection works on the generated rows of the mandatory sheets after the rules that read them: tuples no allowed row contains are counted as infeasible, never as uncovered; both strategies stay greedy and no result claims a minimum (cf.coverage.method has no optimal value).

delta.legacy: The fw_final cut-off was always applied: limitVar, the product of the trailing tables' largest ids that stayed below core.limitVarGivenLessThan, so a product beyond 2^63 kept only its first limitVar rows.
delta.now: cf.assembly.mandatoryLimit applies the same rule when set; its default, 9223372036854775807, means no cut-off, so products of any size stay exact and lazy. An imported legacy value keeps the legacy cut.

delta.legacy: Under FW_VAR the results table had one boolean column per FW_EXIT_CODE carrier sheet, and a failing FW_VAR = k was written into the column at position k minus fwVar.shift (the smallest exit code with results.db.onlyFW_EXIT_CODEcolumns, otherwise 1); the FW_CUSTOM_VAR sheet was copied into the results database when results.db.customvarmapCreateTable was set.
delta.now: Every observation keeps its exact verdict; under cf.execution.verdict=FW_VAR a nonzero verdict names its carrier, the sheet whose FW_EXIT_CODE equals it (attribute carrier), which is where the verdict was set, not a proven cause. Run summaries name verdict codes from the FW_CUSTOM_VAR sheet or the plugin. No table layout remains to choose, so both settings are superseded.

delta.legacy: The in-process executor called a candidate's main with no deadline at all; the sandbox and container runners enforced a wall or CPU limit by killing the child process (destroyForcibly) and reported TIMEOUT.
delta.now: Every attempt has the cooperative deadline cf.execution.timeout.millis: at the deadline the sample's cancellation fires and its thread is interrupted, and a sample that stops within cf.execution.cancel.grace.millis is TIMEOUT (EXEC_DEADLINE). One that does not is TIMEOUT with EXEC_UNCOOPERATIVE and its thread is left running and reported, never killed (one JVM cannot stop it); its late result is ignored. Compilation happens before the deadline starts.

delta.legacy: The executor renamed each candidate's top-level type to C plus its combination id and compiled it with Janino, falling back to ECJ, loading the classes for the run.
delta.now: The JDK compiler (javax.tools) compiles each source in memory under its own declared type name; bytecode is cached by the digest of source, options and class path (cf.compiler.cache.maxBytes), and every sample defines the classes in a fresh class loader, so static fields such as FW_VAR start fresh for every repeat even when the bytecode is reused.

delta.legacy: A candidate's main ran in the executor's own JVM, so a call to System.exit or Runtime.halt in it stopped the executor with every other candidate.
delta.now: Compiled candidates are checked for calls to System.exit, Runtime.exit and Runtime.halt before they run; such a candidate is not run and its sample is BROKEN (EXEC_FORBIDDEN_CALL). Reflection can still reach these methods, which is why execution stays limited to trusted, cooperative code.

delta.legacy: Candidates printed to the executor's own standard streams; an app= metrics line was harvested from a per-candidate sink file.
delta.now: Each attempt's standard output and error are captured with the observation, at most cf.execution.output.maxBytes (truncation is recorded), and reach no console; the metrics line harvest belongs to the results package (M05, audit EX07).

delta.legacy: A blank reader.handoff.runId made the Reader mint a new run id for every run (HandoffManifestWriter.mintRunId).
delta.now: cf.run.id names the run in every sample key; it defaults to 'run', so sample keys are reproducible, and an imported blank keeps that default.

delta.legacy: With K > 1 the legacy executors defaulted to repeatScope=metrics: the first invocation owned the verdict and the other repeats were measurements.
delta.now: cf.execution.repeat.scope defaults to all: every repeat is a verdict sample with its own observation. metrics reproduces the legacy split: repeat 0 is the verdict, the other repeats are measurements counted apart and skipped when repeat 0 gave no verdict.

delta.legacy: fw.controlplane.envs listed executor hosts; work units were dispatched to them and serialised per host.
delta.now: Environments (cf.execution.environments) are labels every sample carries in its key and hands to the system under test; all of them run in this JVM on this host. A legacy host list is refused rather than turned into labels.

delta.legacy: The executor recorded failing samples only (failOnly, its default) or passing ones only (-Dfw.exec.mode=passonly), keeping their sources as attachments.
delta.now: Every observation is committed and counted; cf.results.attach (failed by default, passed, all, none) decides only whose candidate source is kept, within cf.results.maxAttachmentBytes, and an attachment that does not fit is omitted and counted.

delta.legacy: The metrics corpus kept the last line per candidate id (per candidate, repeat and environment when repeat-aware), so a repeated id overwrote another candidate's line.
delta.now: Every sample keeps its line; repeated display ids are ordered by their candidate digest. The line format and the string order are the legacy ones.

delta.legacy: HandoffManifestV2 read integer fields with Number.longValue, truncating fractions, kept the last of a repeated key, and the executor took candidates in the order files arrived.
delta.now: The hand-over import refuses a fractional integer and a repeated key, reads the candidates in a fixed order (by source, then file name), checks candidate_count against the files, refuses Python, sharded and gRPC hand-overs and container policies by name, and writes no results database.

delta.legacy: A launcher re-ran a whole executor with -attempt N, counted from 1 (default 1), to retry it.
delta.now: The run numbers attempts itself, from 0 and one more per retry of TIMEOUT or INFRA_FAIL (cf.execution.retry.maxAttempts); every attempt is kept and the latest per repeat and environment is final.

delta.legacy: fw.controlplane.maxInFlight bounded the work units in flight (default 64); serializePerHost, or a noisy metricSensitivity, let one unit per host run at a time; budgetMillis set a deadline for the whole run.
delta.now: maxInFlight sets cf.execution.workers (at most 1024, coerced with a warning); cf.execution.serialize runs one sample at a time, since every environment shares this host; cf.run.budget.millis cancels the run cooperatively when it passes (RUN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED).

delta.legacy: The batch front skipped points already found dominated, and the batch Pareto path kept only the top 1000 lines by aggregate score before filtering, so a nondominated line could be lost.
delta.now: The front is the definition: every pair is compared, so a missing value (a skipped axis, which makes dominance intransitive) cannot hide a point, and no score prefilter exists; large populations are ranked among the front with that stated. Budgeted analysis admits sample/repeat workspace and metric summaries before allocating them, and counts point/report storage, worst-case dominance relations and NSGA-III/MOEA-D reference directions before those phases allocate. Insufficient budget gives RESOURCE_LIMIT without approximating the front. Input samples and the returned report belong to the caller; temporary operation leases are released on success and failure. The run also admits final-observation snapshots and observation-to-sample adapters before building them, holds those leases through analysis, and charges the retained report through finalization. Completed summaries transfer to their caller; campaigns admit retained history.

delta.legacy: Merging two per-key reservoirs shuffled their union uniformly and kept the first 1024, which over-represents the smaller partition.
delta.now: Each sample's key comes from SHA-256 of the seed, the metric and its identity (weighted A-Res); a merge keeps the largest keys of the union, exactly the sample one pass would keep, whatever the partition or arrival order.

delta.legacy: Simulated annealing reported converged = true after its last iteration; Newton-Raphson returned a bare number; a NaN objective steered the methods.
delta.now: Every method reports its iterations and a convergence it actually tested (annealing reports false); a NaN or infinite objective value stops the method with ANALYSIS_NONFINITE.

evidence.contains: return new MinND(best, fbest, maxIter, true);

delta.legacy: Dynamic objectives were turned into Python code and run with scipy.optimize in a child process; the expression parser reported unknown names only when evaluating.
delta.now: Objectives are typed Java callbacks or the declared expression language, checked when compiled (ANALYSIS_INVALID_EXPRESSION); Python is refused, never run.

delta.legacy: The seed bias joined each winner's candidate id (F_O_J) to the fw_final and fw_opt rows of the Core database to learn its sheet values; a winner whose id did not match was skipped.
delta.now: A seed written by this build carries each winner's sheet selections and the bias reads them; a seed without selections (a legacy seed) cannot bias a scenario (CAMPAIGN_SEED_UNJOINABLE), while the elitism and noop strategies still accept it.

delta.legacy: The full space a bias plan scaled was the Core estimate of the spec times the optional factor (with the product of the sheet sizes when that failed).
delta.now: It is the exact generated count of the run that produced the seed; for a seed read from a file, the product of the sheet sizes (the legacy fallback).

delta.legacy: A bias plan that would keep fewer than one candidate raised SeedBiasError and failed the iterate loop, as did an iteration that produced no seed.
delta.now: Both stop the campaign as EXHAUSTED (CAMPAIGN_EXHAUSTED, a warning) with the iterations before standing; an iteration whose run yields no front winners fails it (CAMPAIGN_NO_WINNERS).

delta.legacy: ElitismStrategy and NoopStrategy were library strategies of the Core that no command wired to the iterate loop; elitism skipped a Seed_ sheet whose exact name existed.
delta.now: cf.campaign.strategy=elitism or noop runs them in a campaign; elitism skips a name that exists ignoring case, because sheet names are compared that way here.

delta.legacy: The Analyzer's shutdown hook wrote the seed to fw.analyzer.seedOutputPath and only printed a failure to standard error.
delta.now: The seed is written atomically when the run completes; a failed write is RESULT_EXPORT_FAILED, reported apart from the run's results and analysis, and the command fails.

delta.legacy: core.seed.inputPath made the Core load a seed and log a summary of it; nothing it generated changed.
delta.now: The imported key is reported as superseded by cf.campaign.seed.input, through which a seed biases a run; importing it changes nothing.

delta.legacy: A run was resumed stage by stage from its journal: finished stages were skipped and a stage still marked RUNNING was refused for manual reconciliation.
delta.now: A run resumes sample by sample from a quiescent checkpoint (written at a drained pause and at the end): its identity is validated, every committed observation restored and only the samples without a final observation run, a cancelled one as its next attempt. A campaign checkpoint also preserves completed iteration reports and lineage, the next seed, derivation inputs and a paused child's run checkpoint; barriers and drained pauses resume with the same canonical lineage as uninterrupted work.

delta.legacy: results_v2 rows named the writing process (java:PID or python:PID) and the bundle policy file; the database kept them in insertion order.
delta.now: export --kind results writes the same columns with worker and policy_id empty (no worker processes, no policy files) and policy_hash the execution policy's digest, ordered by candidate id, repeat, environment and attempt.

delta.legacy: CoverageProbe read whole reports without admission. JaCoCo parsing could throw on oversized counters or wrap a counter sum; coverage.py used Jackson coercion and last duplicate JSON keys; missing reports and malformed JSON silently produced no metrics. JaCoCo extracted ordered attributes with a regex, including counters inside comments, while gcovr's compact lines: syntax was not actually matched.
delta.now: CoverageImport preserves the extraction grammars, last matches, six-decimal fractions, ordinary numeric/string/boolean coercions and metric names. Strict shared JSON rejects duplicate keys, trailing content, excessive nesting and integer literals outside long range; invalid/nonfinite data and overflowing JaCoCo sums discard the report atomically with a warning. Missing/unreadable reports are diagnosed and contribute no metrics. Input/parse and retained provenance require memory admission, RESOURCE_LIMIT stops analysis, and report hashes identify imported bytes. MetricCorpus merges imports before identity checks and never changes verdict eligibility. No external coverage tool is launched.

delta.legacy: OptimizationAnalyzer read its manual JSON through Jackson coercions: a field of the wrong type was ignored, text where a number belonged became a default (1.0 for a token weight, an infinite bound for a quoted range bound), an invalid regular expression was dropped, an objective that did not compile left its goal on the mode, an unknown mode scored nothing. It could execute every line as a shell command and evaluate Python, and could stream through PostgreSQL with several workers. Metrics read with tryParseNumeric kept infinite values. The in-memory path numbered a logical command that the input ended inside by its last physical line (the streamed path by its first).
delta.now: TextScoring keeps the grouping grammar, features, profile, synthesized rules, contribution names and values, notes, matched rules and thresholds: goldens of the unchanged analyzer match exactly. A rules field of the wrong JSON type, non-numeric text where a number belongs, a quoted range bound, an invalid pattern and a duplicate key are INPUT_MALFORMED; an unknown mode is ANALYSIS_INVALID_GOAL; an objective that does not compile is ANALYSIS_INVALID_EXPRESSION. Numbers, numeric text, null bounds (open) and goals without a key (skipped) behave as before. Nothing is executed or evaluated outside Java; one in-memory two-pass analysis, admitted to the memory budget, replaces the database path; infinite metric values are no value; every logical line starts at its first physical line.

delta.legacy: fwgen.parse_spec read spec documents in compatibility mode: an unknown field was printed and ignored, also inside a constraint; a polarity other than forbid or require was printed and read as require; two slots naming one sheet compiled to one data sheet holding the last slot's values; a goal direction other than min or max became a target goal without a value; json.loads kept the last of a repeated key; YAML specs were read with yaml.safe_load; a malformed shape (slots that is not a list, a slot without sheet or values, a string where a list belongs) crashed or was iterated character by character; a byte order mark made the document invalid.
delta.now: SpecReader compiles TOML and JSON specs exactly as fwgen did (the workbook build_compact_core_json made, the sidecar emit_sidecar wrote, the dependency gate, the aliases and every legacy message; all 159 corpus specs match) and keeps the compatibility-mode warnings as INPUT_AUTHORING_WARNING. The constraints then pass the strict sidecar checks the legacy run stage applied to the emitted sidecar, here when the spec is read, so an unknown key or an unknown polarity in a constraint is refused after its warning; two slots declaring one sheet (also ignoring case) are INPUT_DUPLICATE_SHEET; a goal direction other than min or max, a repeated JSON key and a malformed shape are refused with a message; a YAML spec is INPUT_UNSUPPORTED_SYNTAX; a TOML date or time inside a list or table, whose Python repr is not reproduced, is refused; a byte order mark is ignored. Before materialization, expanded values must fit the byte-backed dictionary and a conservative allowance capped at min(256 MiB, heap/4); excess labels are KEY_CENSUS_OVERFLOW and excess expansion storage is RESOURCE_LIMIT. TOML nesting above 128 is INPUT_LIMIT. These input limits supplement, rather than replace, run memory admission. Goals and coverage choices become settings of origin SCENARIO, below every explicit setting.

evidence.contains: the sieve treats it as 'require' (compatibility mode)

delta.legacy: The bundle recorded its stage invariants as database facts and enforce() stopped the stage on the first failed CRITICAL one; BROKEN, TIMEOUT and INFRA_FAIL samples were CRITICAL unless the operator tolerated them (--executor-tolerate-outcomes), so by default a run with any of them failed. Axis coverage and fully excluded values were warnings.
delta.now: Every run report carries one reconciliation of its own totals. A failed consistency check (totals that do not add up) is RUN_RECONCILIATION_FAILED and fails the command, keeping the committed observations. BROKEN, TIMEOUT and INFRA_FAIL samples, abandoned threads, listener losses and values no admitted candidate held are notices in the report (text and XML, with the legacy invariant names); the exit code of a completed run stays 0 as the run contract says, so a gate that wants the legacy behaviour reads the reconciliation's notices or the outcome counts.

evidence.contains: if not r.passed and r.severity == CRITICAL:
return invariants.WARNING if name in tolerated else invariants.CRITICAL

delta.legacy: fwgen predicted each slot's rows from its first verb (FW_Cartes and FW_Group only bounded, an unrecognized verb or a brace operand unknown), kept the post-sieve count as [0, mandatory] unless it enumerated at most 200000 rows, and scaled the final count by assumed per-unit costs (0.05 to 2.0 seconds and fixed byte ranges per candidate) into ESTIMATED duration, database, source, inode, request and optional monetary figures, with S/B/L/X run classes whose limits were command-line options; plan wrote plan.json.
delta.now: plan generates every table lazily, so each table's size is EXACT with its formula and optional rows by length from the operators' parameters (counted while a table is stored). Subset histograms use a binomial recurrence and a local metadata allowance of min(4 MiB, heap/32); omitting an oversized histogram leaves the exact count and previews available. The candidate stages are EXACT when counted within --scan (default 1000000) and a proven range otherwise; admitted, samples, verdicts, measurements and attempts follow the repeat, retry and stop settings, a stop policy or time budget turning them into ranges and an unknown count staying unknown. Duration is ESTIMATED from timeout plus grace and effective parallelism (one for serialized execution); it excludes compilation, queueing, scheduling delays, cleanup, analysis and reporting and is not a wall-clock upper bound. Result and source bytes are ESTIMATED with their assumptions (the first rendered sources as the sample); source sampling is omitted with an UNKNOWN reason when finding survivors could exceed --scan. There are no inode, request or monetary figures (no loose files, no external services, no price). Run classes keep fwgen's default limits (500, 50000, 5000000 samples) without options. The report is the command's text or XML output, with the memory the plan reserved reported apart; the local histogram cap does not establish global budget admission.

delta.legacy: Coverage was measured only by reports that external tools wrote after execution: fw.analyzer.coverage chose a JaCoCo XML, coverage.py JSON or gcov probe reading fw.analyzer.coverageReport for each results line; the Java executor ran the candidates uninstrumented.
delta.now: Reports are still imported (D55). In addition cf.execution.coverage=lines (default none) instruments generated Java candidates in memory with the JDK's class-file API, no agent or subprocess: coverage_line, coverage_line_covered and coverage_line_total count the candidate's own executable source lines (bytecode line tables; synthetic and bridge methods but lambda bodies, an enum's values and valueOf, a record's generated methods and empty no-argument constructors left out) each verdict sample ran, with probes in the attempt's own class loader read once when it completes. The instrumentation version is part of the bytecode cache digest and of the sample's source digest. A candidate without an executable line of its own gets no metric (EXEC_COVERAGE_OMITTED); a plugin run with coverage on is refused (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY).
